A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GEPO/HeteroRL research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v6 reports original Qwen3 mathematical-reasoning experiments, latency analyses, importance-weight ablations and think/non-think comparisons.

after.justification: v8 retains those empirical results and adds asynchronous-baseline comparisons, hyperparameter experiments, an advantage-normalization ablation and empirical bias analysis.

M1.justification: The HeteroRL architecture and GEPO group-expectation weighting in Equations (2)–(3) and Listing 1 are retained. The added explanation of recomputing log-probabilities documents implementation without establishing an algorithm change. Defensive sampling remains future work in both versions.

E1.justification: Both versions train on MATH levels 3–5 and evaluate AMC2023, AIME2024, AIME2025 and MATH500. Online/heterogeneous training, think/non-think modes and lognormal, Weibull and exponential latency scenarios already appear in v6. The added studies remain within this coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds BNPO and Dr.GRPO to the Qwen3-8B heterogeneous comparison, where they were absent in v6. New Appendix K/Table 9 evaluates Truncated IS + KL, TOPR with and without KL, and CISPO with and without KL. The IMPALA-related comparator is its truncated-importance-sampling technique.

E3.justification: Appendix B.1 changes reported gradient accumulation from 1 to 8; the PDFs do not establish reruns of retained results. New Qwen3-1.7B/2k experiments introduce controlled hyperparameter sweeps and KL-augmented baseline comparisons. Table 12 specifies a 60–1920-second latency interval, while B.1 retains 60–1800 seconds.

E4.justification: The original importance-weight ablation moves to Appendix C.1/Table 5 and gains an advantage-normalization control. New analyses examine GEPO versus GSPO bias and sensitivity to group size, KL coefficient, latency distribution, temperature, top-p and top-k. These substantially extend investigation of stability and its conditions.

E5.justification: Appendix J.1 newly documents Monte Carlo bias estimation for GEPO and GSPO and reports summaries over 512 training steps. This adds statistical-estimation documentation, without adding independent-run counts, seeds or benchmark confidence intervals. The earlier correlation-confidence-interval practice is retained.

E6.justification: Existing GEPO headline scores are retained, while substantial new results are reported. Table 9 gives average best/last scores of 40.8/23.3 for TOPR + KL and 43.5/43.5 for GEPO. Table 5 adds normalization results of 43.0/41.5 versus 43.5/43.5 without normalization. Bias measurements and six sensitivity studies add further findings.

T1.justification: New Appendix J introduces bias definitions, Theorem 2's L2-norm-ratio bias bound and Theorem 3's advantage-weighted variance bound, with proofs and additional assumptions. Appendix A's original proof is retained with notation changes. The new variance derivation has a normalization inconsistency in Equation (50).

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims about asynchronous HeteroRL, group-level weighting and high-divergence stability. The headline claims of a 3% latency-related performance drop and an 85% reduction in best-to-last degradation are unchanged.

C2.justification: v8 adds substantive explanations of KL-dependent collapse, group-size regularization, decoding-related stability and the insufficiency of clipping alone. Appendix J argues that policy concentration keeps bias controllable. Existing correlation-versus-causation qualifications and think/non-think tradeoffs remain; the new top-k interpretation partly contradicts Table 15.

D1.justification: v8 newly discloses forward-pass recomputation of log-probabilities to address vLLM/FSDP discrepancies and provides decoding defaults in Appendix L. The stated repository changes from HeteroRL_GEPO to Hetero-RL. Conversely, the evaluation cadence and v6's detailed communication-toolkit feature descriptions are omitted.

R1.justification: Section 5 expands positioning from mainly asynchronous frameworks to a distinction between gradient truncation and importance-weight truncation. It adds Hilton et al., MiniMax-M1/CISPO and TOPR references. Appendix K further explains the relationship to these algorithms and the choice of truncated IS as the IMPALA-related comparator.

P1.justification: Most existing prose remains intact. Changes include renaming Section 4.3, rewriting related work, standardizing Appendix A notation and reorganizing appendices: the weighting discussion and ablation are grouped together, and future work precedes the case study. The main narrative is substantially retained.

P2.justification: v8 adds the six-panel hyperparameter Figure 8, bias Figure 13, asynchronous-training Figure 14 and Tables 8–15. Existing comparison and ablation tables gain rows. The original latency and correlation figures exchange order, and several appendix displays move while retaining their content.

improvement.justification: v8 improves scrutiny of the central stability claim through relevant asynchronous baselines, sensitivity experiments and an advantage-normalization control absent from v6. The net gain is limited by errors in the added support: Equation (50) fails to square the estimator's denominator when computing variance, and the top-k discussion contradicts Table 15. These issues weaken the new theoretical and practical conclusions.
